A critic argues that the earlier version gives readers more frequent opportunities to imagine hesitation, even though both versions convey the same events.
options: The early translation contains events missing from the original novel.
Changes in the division of dialogue can affect how readers perceive a scene without changing its events.
Short exchanges always communicate a character’s intentions more accurately.
The later translation is impossible for modern readers to understand.
acceptedAnswers: Changes in the division of dialogue can affect how readers perceive a scene without changing its events.

explanation.en: The critic links dialogue segmentation to imagined hesitation while explicitly holding events constant. Missing events contradict the passage; incomprehensibility is not discussed; universal superiority of short exchanges exceeds the qualified claim.
explanation.ru: Критик связывает деление реплик с ощущением колебания при одинаковых событиях. Пропущенные события противоречат тексту; непонятность не обсуждается; превосходство коротких реплик во всех случаях не заявлено.

hints.en: Distinguish the content of the scene from the way it is presented.
hints.ru: Различите содержание сцены и способ его подачи.

hints.en: The versions convey the same events but create different pauses.
hints.ru: Версии передают одинаковые события, но создают разные паузы.

typicalErrors.en: Confusing a change in perceived pacing with a change in narrative events.
typicalErrors.ru: Смешение изменения воспринимаемого темпа с изменением событий повествования.

exercises.author: StylishSAT original AI-authored expansion, 2026-09-05; independent expert review pending
exercises.evidence: the earlier version gives readers more frequent opportunities to imagine hesitation, even though both versions convey the same events.

exercises.prompt: Which additional finding would most strengthen the proposed explanation?
exercises.passage: An engineer compared afternoon temperatures on two roofs with the same material and orientation. Roof A had a reflective coating; Roof B did not. A averaged 31°C and B averaged 38°C during the study. The engineer proposes that the coating reduced the amount of heat absorbed by Roof A.
options: Both roofs were visible from the engineer’s office.
Before the coating was applied, the roofs had nearly identical temperatures under comparable weather conditions.
The coating was available in containers of two different sizes.
Roof A had been built several years before Roof B.
acceptedAnswers: Before the coating was applied, the roofs had nearly identical temperatures under comparable weather conditions.

explanation.en: Similar temperatures before treatment make an existing temperature difference less plausible as the explanation. Construction date alone does not show a thermal effect; visibility and container sizes do not test heat absorption. The result strengthens rather than conclusively proves causation.
explanation.ru: Сходные температуры до нанесения покрытия делают прежнее различие менее вероятным объяснением. Возраст сам по себе не показывает теплового эффекта; видимость и размеры упаковки нерелевантны. Это усиливает, но не окончательно доказывает причинный вывод.

hints.en: Ask what alternative explanation a before-treatment comparison could address.
hints.ru: Подумайте, какое альтернативное объяснение проверяет сравнение до обработки.

hints.en: Were the roofs already different in temperature before one received the coating?
hints.ru: Различались ли температуры крыш ещё до покрытия одной из них?

typicalErrors.en: Calling supporting before-treatment evidence conclusive proof of a coating’s causal effect.
typicalErrors.ru: Принятие подтверждающего сравнения до обработки за окончательное доказательство эффекта покрытия.

exercises.author: StylishSAT original AI-authored expansion, 2026-09-05; independent expert review pending
exercises.evidence: the coating reduced the amount of heat absorbed by Roof A.

exercises.prompt: Which inference is most strongly supported?
exercises.passage: Programs from a village choir’s first decade list only the conductor’s name. Payment records from the same years show regular fees to a pianist and a music copyist. A historian cautions against using the programs alone to identify everyone whose work supported the choir.
options: The pianist and copyist performed exactly the same work.
The payment records prove that the conductor did not direct the choir.
The conductor personally paid all of the choir’s expenses.
The programs omit some contributors whose involvement is documented elsewhere.
acceptedAnswers: The programs omit some contributors whose involvement is documented elsewhere.

explanation.en: Fees document at least two unlisted contributors. The records do not identify the payer as the conductor, equate the two jobs, or negate the conductor’s role. The inference concerns incomplete credits, not dishonesty or identical duties.
explanation.ru: Платежи подтверждают участие двух людей, не названных в программах. Не установлено, что платил дирижёр, что обязанности совпадали или что дирижёр не руководил хором. Вывод касается неполноты списка участников.

hints.en: Compare the people identified by the two sources.
hints.ru: Сравните людей, названных в двух источниках.

hints.en: A payment can document participation even when a program gives no credit.
hints.ru: Платёж может подтверждать участие, даже если программа не называет человека.

typicalErrors.en: Inferring exclusive authorship or identical duties from incomplete program credits.
typicalErrors.ru: Вывод об исключительном авторстве или одинаковых обязанностях по неполному списку участников.

exercises.author: StylishSAT original AI-authored expansion, 2026-09-05; independent expert review pending
exercises.evidence: Payment records from the same years show regular fees to a pianist and a music copyist.

exercises.prompt: Which choice most directly supports that suggestion?
exercises.passage: A study counted visits by two bee species to white and purple flowers in equal-sized plots. Species R: 42 visits to white, 18 to purple. Species S: 15 visits to white, 35 to purple. The researchers suggest that combining the species’ counts would hide a difference between their observed visiting patterns.
options: Both species made at least one visit to each flower color.
Species R made 60 visits in total and Species S made 50.
R made more visits to white flowers, whereas S made more visits to purple flowers.
Together the two species made 57 visits to white flowers.
acceptedAnswers: R made more visits to white flowers, whereas S made more visits to purple flowers.

explanation.en: Opposite within-species color patterns demonstrate the difference aggregation could obscure. Visiting both colors does not specify that difference; the combined white count removes species identity; total activity compares quantity rather than color pattern.
explanation.ru: Противоположные соотношения внутри видов показывают различие, которое может скрыться в сумме. Посещение обоих цветов этого не показывает; общий счёт белых стирает вид; общая активность сравнивает количество, а не выбор цвета.

hints.en: The claim concerns a difference in patterns, not just totals.
hints.ru: Утверждение касается различий закономерностей, а не только сумм.

hints.en: Compare white with purple separately for each species.
hints.ru: Сравните белые и фиолетовые цветы отдельно для каждого вида.

typicalErrors.en: Using a combined flower-visit count when the claim concerns opposite within-species patterns.
typicalErrors.ru: Использование общей суммы посещений, когда тезис касается противоположных закономерностей внутри видов.

exercises.author: StylishSAT original AI-authored expansion, 2026-09-05; independent expert review pending
exercises.evidence: Species R: 42 visits to white, 18 to purple. Species S: 15 visits to white, 35 to purple.

exercises.prompt: Which inference about Ivo is best supported by the text?
exercises.passage: After decades away, Ivo returned to the harbor of his childhood. The warehouse had become apartments and the narrow pier was gone. Yet when a rope struck a mast in the breeze, he stopped searching for familiar buildings. For a moment, he felt that he knew exactly where he was.
options: He concluded that the harbor’s buildings had changed very little.
He decided to buy an apartment in the former warehouse.
He could no longer remember how the pier had once looked.
A familiar sound restored a sense of connection that the altered buildings had not provided.
acceptedAnswers: A familiar sound restored a sense of connection that the altered buildings had not provided.

explanation.en: The sound follows unsuccessful searching and immediately produces recognition. The buildings explicitly changed; a purchase decision is absent; the text describes a missing pier without establishing failure to remember it.
explanation.ru: После поиска знакомых зданий звук сразу вызывает узнавание. Здания явно изменились; покупка не обсуждается; отсутствие причала не означает, что герой его не помнит.

hints.en: Trace what happens immediately before his feeling changes.
hints.ru: Проследите, что непосредственно предшествует изменению чувства героя.

hints.en: The turning point is the rope striking the mast.
hints.ru: Переломный момент — удар верёвки о мачту.

typicalErrors.en: Attributing recognition to unchanged buildings when a sound triggers it.
typicalErrors.ru: Приписывание узнавания неизменным зданиям, хотя его вызывает звук.

exercises.author: StylishSAT original AI-authored expansion, 2026-09-05; independent expert review pending
exercises.evidence: Yet when a rope struck a mast in the breeze, he stopped searching for familiar buildings.

exercises.prompt: Which finding would most directly support the second researcher’s caution?
exercises.passage: An archaeologist argues that bowls found at an inland settlement were imported from a coastal workshop because their clay contains a mineral uncommon inland. Another researcher notes that identifying a material’s origin does not necessarily identify where an object was manufactured.
options: Unfired blocks of coastal clay and a kiln containing unfinished bowls were found at the inland settlement.
The coastal region contained more than one clay deposit.
The coastal workshop stood near a route leading inland.
Several finished bowls had decorative bands around their rims.
acceptedAnswers: Unfired blocks of coastal clay and a kiln containing unfinished bowls were found at the inland settlement.

explanation.en: Imported raw clay plus local production equipment gives a concrete route to making bowls inland from coastal material. Decoration does not locate production; a trade route fits imports of either clay or finished bowls; multiple coastal deposits do not establish inland manufacture.
explanation.ru: Привозная сырая глина и местное производство показывают возможность изготовления внутри страны из прибрежного материала. Украшение не указывает место; путь подходит и для глины, и для готовых мисок; несколько прибрежных залежей не доказывают местного изготовления.

hints.en: Distinguish moving raw material from moving a finished object.
hints.ru: Различите перевозку сырья и готового изделия.

hints.en: Look for evidence that coastal clay could have been shaped and fired inland.
hints.ru: Ищите свидетельства обработки и обжига прибрежной глины внутри страны.

typicalErrors.en: Treating the origin of raw clay as necessarily the manufacturing location of a bowl.
typicalErrors.ru: Принятие происхождения сырой глины за обязательное место изготовления миски.

exercises.author: StylishSAT original AI-authored expansion, 2026-09-05; independent expert review pending
exercises.evidence: identifying a material’s origin does not necessarily identify where an object was manufactured.

exercises.prompt: Which statement best captures the conclusion?
exercises.passage: Researchers grew one plant variety under either steady light or light alternating between bright and dim intervals. Both groups received the same total daily light. The alternating-light group developed smaller leaves. The researchers conclude that the distribution of light over time deserves attention alongside its daily total.
options: Equal total light exposure need not produce the same leaf development when the timing of exposure differs.
Leaf size depends only on the variety of plant being grown.
Steady light prevents every kind of variation in plant development.
Plants under alternating light received less total daily light.
acceptedAnswers: Equal total light exposure need not produce the same leaf development when the timing of exposure differs.

explanation.en: The experiment holds daily light and variety constant while timing and leaf size differ. Less total light contradicts the setup; variety alone cannot explain a difference within one variety; a universal claim about steady light is unsupported.
explanation.ru: Суточное количество света и сорт постоянны, а режим и размер листьев различаются. Меньшее количество света противоречит условиям; один сорт не объясняет различие; универсальный вывод о постоянном свете не подтверждён.

hints.en: Separate the total amount from the schedule of exposure.
hints.ru: Различите суммарное количество и режим освещения.

hints.en: Both groups received equal daily totals but developed different leaf sizes.
hints.ru: Суточные суммы одинаковы, но размеры листьев различны.

typicalErrors.en: Equating total light with its distribution over time.
typicalErrors.ru: Приравнивание общего количества света к его распределению во времени.

exercises.author: StylishSAT original AI-authored expansion, 2026-09-05; independent expert review pending
exercises.evidence: Both groups received the same total daily light. The alternating-light group developed smaller leaves.

exercises.prompt: Which finding would most directly challenge the manager’s attribution?
exercises.passage: A theater lowered the price of weekday tickets. The following month, weekday attendance rose. The manager attributes the entire rise to the lower price, but the theater also introduced a weekday shuttle from a nearby university at the start of that month.
options: Many new weekday attendees said they had previously been unable to reach the theater and used the new shuttle.
The theater continued to perform plays on weekends.
Some audience members had attended the theater for years.
The reduced ticket price was printed on the theater’s website.
acceptedAnswers: Many new weekday attendees said they had previously been unable to reach the theater and used the new shuttle.

explanation.en: The shuttle enabled attendance for new visitors, offering a competing contributor to the increase. Weekend performances and advertising the price do not challenge the price explanation; existing attendees do not explain the new attendance. The evidence challenges “entire,” not any possible price effect.
explanation.ru: Автобус позволил новым зрителям приехать и даёт альтернативный вклад в рост. Спектакли выходного дня и публикация цены этого не показывают; давние зрители не объясняют прибавку. Оспаривается слово entire, а не любой эффект цены.

hints.en: Look for another change that could have enabled additional visits.
hints.ru: Ищите другое изменение, позволившее увеличить посещаемость.

hints.en: The strongest evidence connects the shuttle specifically to new attendees.
hints.ru: Самое сильное свидетельство связывает автобус именно с новыми зрителями.

typicalErrors.en: Ignoring a concurrent transport change when explaining the entire attendance increase.
typicalErrors.ru: Игнорирование одновременного изменения транспорта при объяснении всего роста посещаемости.

exercises.author: StylishSAT original AI-authored expansion, 2026-09-05; independent expert review pending
exercises.evidence: the theater also introduced a weekday shuttle from a nearby university at the start of that month.

exercises.prompt: Which statement is most strongly supported?
exercises.passage: A conservation team cleaned one narrow strip of a darkened mural. Bright yellow shapes appeared beneath the surface deposit. The team has not yet cleaned the rest of the mural and warns that the test strip should not be treated as a complete guide to the original color scheme.
options: The yellow shapes were painted onto the mural during cleaning.
The strip establishes that some yellow shapes were obscured, but the colors elsewhere remain to be determined.
The entire mural originally consisted only of bright yellow shapes.
Cleaning the rest of the mural will certainly damage its surface.
acceptedAnswers: The strip establishes that some yellow shapes were obscured, but the colors elsewhere remain to be determined.

explanation.en: The observed yellow supports a local conclusion; uncleaned areas remain unknown. Extending yellow to the entire mural overgeneralizes, damage is not predicted, and the text says the shapes appeared beneath a deposit rather than being added.
explanation.ru: Жёлтые фигуры подтверждены только на очищенном участке; остальные области пока неизвестны. Распространение цвета на всю роспись чрезмерно; повреждение не предсказано; фигуры находились под налётом, а не были дорисованы.

hints.en: Distinguish what was observed from what has not yet been examined.
hints.ru: Различите наблюдаемое и ещё не исследованное.

hints.en: Only a narrow strip has been cleaned.
hints.ru: Очищена только узкая полоса.

typicalErrors.en: Extending findings from one cleaned strip to an entire unexamined mural.
typicalErrors.ru: Распространение результата одной очищенной полосы на неисследованную роспись целиком.

exercises.author: StylishSAT original AI-authored expansion, 2026-09-05; independent expert review pending
exercises.evidence: The team has not yet cleaned the rest of the mural

exercises.prompt: Which finding would most directly support the proposed explanation?
exercises.passage: A researcher interviewed vendors at a night market about their use of reusable containers. Several vendors who had stopped using them described limited washing space as a difficulty. The researcher proposes that access to washing facilities, rather than vendors’ awareness of waste, may help explain differences in container use.
options: Reusable containers came in a wider range of colors than disposable ones.
Vendors with similar knowledge of waste issues used reusable containers more often when they had convenient washing facilities.
Most vendors could name more than one type of packaging.
Some customers arrived at the market before sunset.
acceptedAnswers: Vendors with similar knowledge of waste issues used reusable containers more often when they had convenient washing facilities.

explanation.en: The key varies facility access while keeping awareness similar, matching the proposed explanation. Naming packaging does not compare actual use by washing access; arrival time and color range do not test either proposed factor.
explanation.ru: Ключ сравнивает доступ к мойке при сходной осведомлённости. Знание видов упаковки не сопоставляет реальное использование с мойкой; время прихода и цвета не проверяют объяснение.

hints.en: Identify which competing factor should be kept similar.
hints.ru: Определите, какой конкурирующий фактор нужно удержать сходным.

hints.en: Compare actual container use among equally informed vendors with different washing access.
hints.ru: Сравните использование тары у одинаково осведомлённых продавцов с разным доступом к мойке.

typicalErrors.en: Comparing awareness without connecting washing access to actual container use.
typicalErrors.ru: Сравнение осведомлённости без связи доступа к мойке с реальным использованием тары.

exercises.author: StylishSAT original AI-authored expansion, 2026-09-05; independent expert review pending
exercises.evidence: access to washing facilities, rather than vendors’ awareness of waste, may help explain differences in container use.

exercises.prompt: Which conclusion is most strongly supported by the second team’s findings?
exercises.passage: A team detected traces of a compound in moss collected near a workshop and proposed that the workshop released the compound into the air. A second team found the same compound in unused collection vials from the first team’s supply. Blank vials carried through transport and laboratory processing also tested positive.
options: All environmental measurements using glass vials are invalid.
The original measurements cannot by themselves establish that the compound in the samples came from the workshop.
The moss must naturally produce the compound in large quantities.
The workshop definitely released none of the compound during the collection period.
acceptedAnswers: The original measurements cannot by themselves establish that the compound in the samples came from the workshop.

explanation.en: Positive unused and processed blanks provide a possible contamination source independent of the workshop. They do not prove zero workshop emissions, natural moss production, or failure of every glass-vial study. The supported conclusion limits what these measurements establish.
explanation.ru: Положительные пустые пробирки указывают на возможное загрязнение независимо от мастерской. Это не доказывает нулевых выбросов, естественного производства мхом или непригодности всех стеклянных пробирок. Вывод ограничивает доказательную силу этих измерений.

hints.en: Ask whether the detected signal necessarily originated in the collected moss.
hints.ru: Проверьте, обязательно ли обнаруженное вещество происходило из собранного мха.

hints.en: Even blanks with no moss tested positive.
hints.ru: Даже пустые пробы без мха дали положительный результат.

typicalErrors.en: Treating possible vial contamination as proof that the workshop emitted nothing.
typicalErrors.ru: Принятие возможного загрязнения пробирок за доказательство отсутствия выбросов мастерской.

exercises.author: StylishSAT original AI-authored expansion, 2026-09-05; independent expert review pending
exercises.evidence: Blank vials carried through transport and laboratory processing also tested positive.

exercises.prompt: Which explanation best accounts for the analyst’s observation?
exercises.passage: An archive changed its request system. Under the old system, 40 of 50 simple requests and 10 of 50 complex requests were completed within a week. Under the new system, 9 of 10 simple requests and 27 of 90 complex requests were completed within a week. An analyst notes that performance improved within each request category although the overall completion percentage fell.
options: The new system’s requests included a much larger share of the harder-to-complete category.
The completion percentage for simple requests fell under the new system.
The total number of requests doubled after the system changed.
Complex requests became more likely than simple requests to finish within a week.
acceptedAnswers: The new system’s requests included a much larger share of the harder-to-complete category.

explanation.en: Within-category rates rise from 80% to 90% and 20% to 30%, but complex requests rise from half to nine tenths of the total. Overall completion therefore falls from 50% to 36%. Complex never exceeds simple; each total is 100; the simple rate rises.
explanation.ru: Внутри групп доли растут с 80% до 90% и с 20% до 30%, но сложные запросы занимают уже 9/10 вместо 1/2. Общая доля падает с 50% до 36%. Сложные не превосходят простые; оба итога равны 100; доля простых растёт.

hints.en: Compare both the success rates and the sizes of the two categories.
hints.ru: Сравните и доли выполнения, и размеры двух групп.

hints.en: The category with the lower completion rate forms 90 of the 100 new requests.
hints.ru: Группа с меньшей долей выполнения составляет 90 из 100 новых запросов.

typicalErrors.en: Comparing overall completion rates without checking changes in category composition.
typicalErrors.ru: Сравнение общих долей выполнения без учёта изменения состава категорий.

exercises.author: StylishSAT original AI-authored expansion, 2026-09-05; independent expert review pending
exercises.evidence: Under the new system, 9 of 10 simple requests and 27 of 90 complex requests were completed within a week.

exercises.prompt: Which hypothetical finding would most directly resolve the specific uncertainty the scholar identifies?
exercises.passage: Two surviving copies of a poem end differently. Copy A ends with the speaker leaving a garden; Copy B ends with the speaker returning to its gate. A dated letter quotes Copy B’s ending, but Copy A itself has no date. A scholar argues that the letter establishes that B’s ending existed by that date, while leaving the order in which the endings were composed unresolved.
options: A bookseller’s list shows that both surviving copies were sold in the same year.
An analysis shows that both copies use the same type of paper.
A review praises the emotional effect of the return ending.
A dated author’s draft labels the departure ending as a revision of the earlier return ending.
acceptedAnswers: A dated author’s draft labels the departure ending as a revision of the earlier return ending.

explanation.en: The explicit revision relationship orders the composition of the endings. A shared sale year dates circulation, not composition; matching paper does not order writing; aesthetic praise does not date either version. The finding need not establish which surviving physical copy is older.
explanation.ru: Явная помета о переработке устанавливает порядок создания концовок. Год продажи датирует обращение, не сочинение; одинаковая бумага не задаёт порядок; оценка эффекта не датирует версии. Возраст самих сохранившихся экземпляров здесь не требуется.

hints.en: Name the unresolved chronology precisely.
hints.ru: Точно назовите неустановленную последовательность.

hints.en: Look for evidence about one ending being composed before the other.
hints.ru: Ищите свидетельство создания одной концовки раньше другой.

typicalErrors.en: Using sale dates, paper similarity, or praise to infer the order of composition.
typicalErrors.ru: Вывод о порядке сочинения по датам продажи, сходству бумаги или похвале.

exercises.author: StylishSAT original AI-authored expansion, 2026-09-05; independent expert review pending
exercises.evidence: leaving the order in which the endings were composed unresolved.

exercises.prompt: Which statement best explains how the experiment supports the suggestion?
exercises.passage: A fungus was once thought to benefit a tree simply by increasing its water supply. In an experiment, trees with and without the fungus received enough water to maintain equal leaf water levels. Trees with the fungus nevertheless grew faster. Their roots also absorbed more phosphorus. The researchers suggest that the fungus’s contribution is not limited to water provision.
options: Trees without the fungus absorbed no phosphorus at all.
Equal leaf water levels demonstrate that phosphorus caused every difference in growth.
The growth difference persisted when measured water status was equal, and another potentially beneficial difference was observed.
The fungus must reduce tree growth whenever water becomes scarce.
acceptedAnswers: The growth difference persisted when measured water status was equal, and another potentially beneficial difference was observed.

explanation.en: Equal measured water status weakens a water-only account; greater phosphorus uptake supplies a plausible additional pathway. It does not prove exclusive phosphorus causation, zero uptake without fungus, or any prediction about drought. “Not limited” is weaker than “only phosphorus.”
explanation.ru: Равный измеренный водный статус ослабляет объяснение только водой; большее усвоение фосфора даёт дополнительный возможный механизм. Это не доказывает единственной причины, нулевого усвоения без гриба или эффекта засухи. «Не только вода» не равно «только фосфор».

hints.en: Separate evidence against an exclusive explanation from proof of a single replacement.
hints.ru: Различите опровержение исключительного объяснения и доказательство одной новой причины.

hints.en: Growth still differed when leaf water levels were equal.
hints.ru: Рост различался даже при одинаковом содержании воды в листьях.

typicalErrors.en: Replacing a water-only explanation with an unproved phosphorus-only explanation.
typicalErrors.ru: Замена объяснения только водой недоказанным объяснением только фосфором.

exercises.author: StylishSAT original AI-authored expansion, 2026-09-05; independent expert review pending
exercises.evidence: Trees with the fungus nevertheless grew faster. Their roots also absorbed more phosphorus.

exercises.prompt: Which inference is best supported by the notebook?
exercises.passage: A historian proposes that a bellfounder adopted a lighter alloy to make bells easier to transport. Surviving orders show that the new alloy first appeared in bells sold to distant customers. However, a newly recovered notebook records that the foundry tested the alloy on small, locally delivered bells for several years before offering it in larger bells.
options: The alloy made bells heavier than those produced by the previous method.
The first surviving distant orders may not reflect when or why the foundry initially adopted the alloy.
The foundry stopped selling bells locally before testing the new alloy.
Distant customers necessarily requested the original alloy experiments.
acceptedAnswers: The first surviving distant orders may not reflect when or why the foundry initially adopted the alloy.

explanation.en: Earlier local tests separate the surviving sales pattern from initial adoption, leaving motive unresolved. The notebook says nothing about increased weight, contradicts the claim that local sales had stopped, and does not connect distant customers to the experiments.
explanation.ru: Ранние местные испытания отделяют картину сохранившихся заказов от начала освоения; мотив остаётся неизвестным. Рост массы не указан; местные поставки прямо упомянуты; связи дальних клиентов с испытаниями нет.

hints.en: Compare the timing and setting of the experiments with those of surviving sales.
hints.ru: Сравните время и место испытаний с сохранившимися продажами.

hints.en: Local trials preceded the distant orders used to infer the original motive.
hints.ru: Местные испытания предшествовали дальним заказам, по которым вывели исходный мотив.

typicalErrors.en: Assuming the earliest surviving sales record identifies the original adoption motive.
typicalErrors.ru: Предположение, что ранняя сохранившаяся продажа устанавливает исходный мотив внедрения.

exercises.prompt: Which choice most directly supports the colleague’s caution?
exercises.passage: A passage between two pools allows fish to move upstream. Researchers counted 60 crossings during a high-water week and 20 during a low-water week. The estimated number of fish approaching the passage was 300 in the high-water week and 50 in the low-water week. A colleague cautions that crossing counts alone give a misleading impression of passage success.
options: The low-water week had fewer crossings and therefore a lower crossing proportion.
Exactly the same number of fish approached in both weeks.
The data show that every individual fish prefers low water.
Although more fish crossed during high water, a smaller proportion of approaching fish crossed then.
acceptedAnswers: Although more fish crossed during high water, a smaller proportion of approaching fish crossed then.

explanation.en: Crossing proportions are 60/300 = 20% and 20/50 = 40%, reversing the raw-count comparison. Fewer crossings need not mean a lower proportion; approach counts differ; aggregate success does not establish every fish’s preference or a causal water effect.
explanation.ru: Доли равны 60/300 = 20% и 20/50 = 40%, что обращает сравнение абсолютных чисел. Меньшее число не означает меньшую долю; число подошедших различается; групповые данные не доказывают предпочтение каждой рыбы или причинный эффект воды.

hints.en: Use the number approaching as the denominator.
hints.ru: Используйте число подошедших рыб как знаменатель.

hints.en: Compare 60 out of 300 with 20 out of 50.
hints.ru: Сравните 60 из 300 и 20 из 50.

typicalErrors.en: Comparing crossing counts without dividing by the number of approaching fish.
typicalErrors.ru: Сравнение числа переходов без деления на число подошедших рыб.

exercises.prompt: Which conclusion best integrates the evidence?
exercises.passage: A biographer describes a novelist as a solitary worker because her published essays praise writing in seclusion. Yet drafts contain comments in another person’s handwriting, and letters acknowledge that this reader suggested changes to several endings. The biographer revises the account while retaining the claim that the novelist valued private time to compose.
options: The novelist could value solitary composition while also relying on another reader during revision.
The handwritten comments show that the other reader wrote the published novels entirely.
The letters prove that the novelist never worked alone.
The published essays must have been composed by the reader who commented on the drafts.
acceptedAnswers: The novelist could value solitary composition while also relying on another reader during revision.

explanation.en: Composition and revision can involve different working arrangements, reconciling the evidence. Suggestions about endings do not establish complete authorship, rule out all solitary work, or identify the essay author as anyone other than the novelist.
explanation.ru: Сочинение и редактирование могут проходить по-разному, что согласует источники. Советы по концовкам не означают полного авторства, не исключают работу в одиночестве и не приписывают эссе другому читателю.

hints.en: Consider whether the sources describe different stages of writing.
hints.ru: Подумайте, описывают ли источники разные этапы работы.

hints.en: Private composition does not exclude outside comments on a draft.
hints.ru: Самостоятельное сочинение не исключает чужих замечаний к черновику.

typicalErrors.en: Treating solitary drafting and collaborative revision as mutually exclusive.
typicalErrors.ru: Принятие самостоятельного сочинения и совместного редактирования за несовместимые процессы.

exercises.prompt: Which result would most specifically support the proposed role of resemblance to the distasteful species?
exercises.passage: A biologist proposes that a harmless beetle’s striped pattern discourages predators because it resembles a distasteful species. In a planned experiment, identical edible models will be painted either with the beetle’s stripes or with a plain pattern. Predators from regions with and without the distasteful species will be tested separately.
options: Predators familiar with the distasteful species avoided striped models more than plain models, while unfamiliar predators attacked both patterns at similar rates.
Unfamiliar predators attacked plain models more often than familiar predators did, with no results reported for striped models.
All predators avoided every model regardless of pattern or region.
Striped models weighed slightly less than plain models before painting.
acceptedAnswers: Predators familiar with the distasteful species avoided striped models more than plain models, while unfamiliar predators attacked both patterns at similar rates.

explanation.en: The interaction between pattern and prior regional exposure matches learned resemblance-based avoidance. Universal avoidance cannot isolate the pattern; weight is not the proposed cue and violates identical-model intent; a plain-only comparison never tests stripes against plain within groups.
explanation.ru: Совместная зависимость от рисунка и знакомства с неприятным видом соответствует объяснению через сходство. Всеобщее избегание не выделяет рисунок; масса не является предполагаемым сигналом; сравнение только однотонных моделей вообще не проверяет полосы.

hints.en: The explanation predicts more than a general aversion to stripes.
hints.ru: Объяснение предсказывает больше, чем общее избегание полос.

hints.en: Look for a stripe advantage specifically among predators familiar with the distasteful species.
hints.ru: Ищите преимущество полос именно у хищников, знакомых с неприятным видом.

typicalErrors.en: Selecting a general avoidance result that cannot isolate familiarity-dependent mimicry.
typicalErrors.ru: Выбор общего избегания, не выделяющего зависимость подражания от знакомства с видом.

exercises.prompt: Which choice best expresses the historian’s interpretation?
exercises.passage: Letters written during construction of an embankment complain about blocked footpaths but rarely mention flooding. Later commemorative accounts describe flood prevention as the project’s defining benefit. A historian argues that these sources answer different questions: the letters illuminate immediate disruption, while commemorations select outcomes that later communities considered worth remembering.
options: The sources cannot both be useful because they mention different aspects of the project.
The commemorative accounts establish that no residents opposed the project.
Differences in the sources’ purposes and time perspectives can explain their different emphases.
The letters prove that flooding had never occurred before construction.
acceptedAnswers: Differences in the sources’ purposes and time perspectives can explain their different emphases.

explanation.en: The historian treats immediate experience and later commemoration as complementary perspectives. Silence about flooding does not prove its absence; praising benefits does not erase opposition; different emphases are precisely why both sources can be useful.
explanation.ru: Историк рассматривает непосредственный опыт и позднее воспоминание как дополняющие перспективы. Молчание о наводнениях не доказывает их отсутствия; похвала не отменяет возражений; разные акценты как раз делают оба источника полезными.

hints.en: Ask what each kind of source was trying to communicate.
hints.ru: Определите, что стремился передать каждый тип источника.

hints.en: One source records disruption as it happens; the other commemorates selected later significance.
hints.ru: Один источник фиксирует текущие неудобства, другой — позднее выбранное значение события.

typicalErrors.en: Treating silence or selective commemoration as proof that an event or opposition never existed.
typicalErrors.ru: Принятие молчания или выборочного воспоминания за доказательство отсутствия события или возражений.

exercises.prompt: Which conclusion is most directly supported?
exercises.passage: To test whether a grass stabilizes dunes through its roots rather than through its aboveground stems, researchers compared three treatments: intact grass, grass with stems clipped but roots left alive, and bare sand with neither roots nor stems. After identical wind exposure, average sand loss was 4, 5, and 18 grams, respectively.
options: Clipping the stems increased sand loss by 14 grams compared with intact grass.
Living roots prevent all movement of sand under every wind condition.
Aboveground stems are necessary for any reduction in sand loss.
Living roots appear to account for much of the reduced sand loss under the tested conditions.
acceptedAnswers: Living roots appear to account for much of the reduced sand loss under the tested conditions.

explanation.en: Root-only plots lost 5 grams, close to intact plots’ 4 and far below bare sand’s 18, supporting a substantial root contribution. Clipped plots still reduce loss; clipping adds 1 gram, not 14; nonzero loss and one tested wind condition rule out absolute prevention.
explanation.ru: Участки с корнями потеряли 5 г против 4 г у целых растений и 18 г у голого песка: вклад корней велик. Срезанные растения всё ещё уменьшают потери; срезание добавляет 1 г, не 14; ненулевые потери и один режим ветра исключают абсолютную гарантию.

hints.en: Compare the clipped treatment with both the intact and bare treatments.
hints.ru: Сравните срезанные растения и с целыми, и с голым песком.

hints.en: Removing stems changes loss only slightly; removing both roots and stems changes it much more.
hints.ru: Удаление стеблей мало меняет потери; отсутствие и корней, и стеблей меняет их намного сильнее.

typicalErrors.en: Confusing the intact-versus-bare difference with the intact-versus-clipped difference.
typicalErrors.ru: Смешение различия между целыми растениями и голым песком с различием между целыми и срезанными растениями.

exercises.passage: The field researcher did not begin by asking residents to complete a long survey. Instead, she attended neighborhood meetings and answered questions about her project. She hoped to cultivate trust before requesting detailed accounts of people’s experiences.

explanation.en: Meetings and answers are intended to build trust. Harvest invokes a literal crop sense; concealing trust opposes the effort to build a relationship; evaluating trust would measure it rather than establish it.
explanation.ru: Встречи и ответы должны укрепить доверие. Harvest относится к сбору урожая; conceal — скрывать — не соответствует созданию отношений; evaluate означает оценить, а не сформировать доверие.

hints.en: Ask what the researcher wants her preliminary actions to accomplish.

hints.en: She wants trust to grow before she asks for personal accounts.

exercises.prompt: What is the main purpose of the text?
exercises.passage: A curator’s exhibition pairs repaired household objects with the stories of people who repaired them. A teacup appears beside an account of a child learning to mend its handle; a patched coat is accompanied by its owner’s description of wearing it for twenty winters. Together, the displays present repair as part of a continuing relationship with possessions.

To compare the market prices of two damaged household items.
To give step-by-step instructions for repairing a coat.
To explain how an exhibition connects repaired objects with people’s experiences.
acceptedAnswers: To explain how an exhibition connects repaired objects with people’s experiences.

explanation.en: The examples illustrate the exhibition’s interpretive connection between objects and lives. There are no repair instructions, no dismissal of use outside museums, and no price comparison.
explanation.ru: Примеры показывают связь вещей с жизненным опытом в экспозиции. Инструкций по ремонту нет; ценность вне музея не отрицается; цены не сравниваются.

hints.en: Identify what the examples of the cup and coat illustrate.

hints.en: Both objects are displayed with a personal account.
hints.ru: Оба предмета сопровождаются личным рассказом.

typicalErrors.en: Confusing examples in an exhibition description with repair instructions.
typicalErrors.ru: Подмена примеров описания выставки инструкцией по ремонту.

exercises.prompt: What is the function of the final sentence?
exercises.passage: The old theater’s backstage floors slope gently toward a central drain. This feature can puzzle visitors who expect an entirely level work area. The building once housed a laundry, where water had to flow away from the washing stations.
options: It disputes the claim that the floors are sloped.
It lists all the changes made when the theater opened.
It explains a feature introduced earlier by describing the building’s former use.
It recommends converting the theater back into a laundry.
acceptedAnswers: It explains a feature introduced earlier by describing the building’s former use.

explanation.en: The former laundry use explains why drainage influenced the floor. It confirms rather than denies the physical feature, recommends no conversion, and does not list renovations.

The allocation of space suggests that, for Leena, an object’s interest need not correspond to its physical size.
options: It states a rule for drawing accurately and then proves that Leena follows it.
It presents a disagreement between two artists and then settles it.
It contrasts two kinds of depiction and then offers an interpretation of that contrast.
It narrates the city square’s construction in chronological order.
acceptedAnswers: It contrasts two kinds of depiction and then offers an interpretation of that contrast.

exercises.passage:
Text 1: A simplified transit map omits many street bends so riders can quickly see where to change lines. Its usefulness depends on selecting the details relevant to that task.

Text 2: A walking map needs to show street bends and distances because pedestrians must follow the route on the ground. The appropriate amount of detail depends on what the map is meant to help someone do.
options: A map becomes useless if it leaves out any detail.
A map’s intended use should influence which details it includes.
Transit maps are always more accurate than walking maps.
Every map should reproduce every street bend.
acceptedAnswers: A map’s intended use should influence which details it includes.

explanation.en: Both authors tie detail to purpose. Text 1 explicitly allows omitted bends; neither ranks overall accuracy; usefulness despite selective omission contradicts the last choice.
explanation.ru: Оба автора связывают детализацию с задачей. Первый допускает пропуск изгибов; общую точность карт никто не ранжирует; полезность выборочного изображения противоречит последнему варианту.

hints.en: Look for a principle that applies to both kinds of map.

hints.en: Each author chooses details according to the user’s task.
hints.ru: Каждый автор выбирает детали в соответствии с задачей пользователя.

typicalErrors.ru: Предположение, что полезные карты должны включать одинаковые детали независимо от цели.

exercises.prompt: How would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the recommendation in Text 1?
exercises.passage:
Text 1: Gardeners in our valley should follow the same planting date each year. A fixed date makes seasonal work easier to organize.

Text 2: The last frost in our valley varies greatly from year to year. Gardeners who adjust planting to current conditions can avoid exposing tender seedlings to an unusually late frost.
options: A fixed date prevents late frosts from occurring in the valley.
A fixed date may simplify planning but fail to account for changing frost conditions.
The valley’s frost conditions never influence young plants.
Gardeners should stop organizing their work in advance altogether.
acceptedAnswers: A fixed date may simplify planning but fail to account for changing frost conditions.

explanation.en: Text 2 identifies annual variation that a fixed date misses; the response can concede organizational convenience without accepting the recommendation. Planting dates do not control weather; seedlings are vulnerable; adjusting plans is not abandoning planning.
explanation.ru: Второй текст указывает на изменчивость, которую фиксированная дата не учитывает, допуская её удобство. Даты не управляют погодой; всходы уязвимы; корректировка плана не равна отказу от планирования.

hints.en: Identify the variable considered in Text 2 but not in Text 1.
hints.ru: Определите переменную, учтённую во втором тексте, но не в первом.

hints.en: The last frost does not arrive on the same date every year.
hints.ru: Последний заморозок бывает в разные даты.

typicalErrors.en: Interpreting flexible planting plans as an abandonment of all advance planning.
typicalErrors.ru: Принятие гибкого плана посадок за отказ от любого предварительного планирования.

exercises.prompt: What is the function of the comparison with people linking arms?
exercises.passage: A fabric’s strength depends partly on the way its threads cross. A single thread may slide easily, but crossing threads repeatedly makes such movement more difficult. Think of people linking arms in several directions: an individual cannot step away without affecting the others.
options: It introduces a separate argument about the benefits of group exercise.
It shows that individual threads become physically thicker when woven.
It makes the restraining effect of interwoven threads easier to visualize.
It proves that fabric and human muscles have the same chemical composition.

exercises.prompt: Which statement would both authors most likely endorse?

explanation.en: Common-source dependence reduces the number of independent attestations, qualifying standardization evidence. The logs can still inform other questions; written copying says nothing decisive about speech; identical wording does not establish different coastlines.

hints.en: Ask whether multiple documents necessarily mean multiple independent observations.

hints.ru: Скопированные описания могут происходить из одного путеводителя.

typicalErrors.en: Counting copied documents as independent attestations of widespread usage.
typicalErrors.ru: Подсчёт скопированных документов как независимых подтверждений распространённого употребления.

exercises.prompt: Which conclusion about Text 1 would the author of Text 2 most likely support?
exercises.passage:
Text 1: Students who moved their hands while learning a new spatial rule later explained it more accurately. The movements may have helped them represent relationships that were difficult to express in words alone.

Text 2: In our experiment, students who watched another person make the relevant movements improved even when they kept their own hands still. Producing a movement may be one useful route to learning, but observing its spatial structure can also help.

Its explanation proves that all verbal instruction should be eliminated.
Its findings establish that watching another person’s movements cannot improve learning.
Its proposed benefit of movement is plausible, but learners need not produce the movements themselves to gain a benefit.
acceptedAnswers: Its proposed benefit of movement is plausible, but learners need not produce the movements themselves to gain a benefit.

explanation.en: Text 2 explicitly allows producing movements as one route and supplies observation as another. It does not attribute prior knowledge, deny its own observation result, or reject all verbal instruction.
explanation.ru: Второй текст допускает собственные движения как один путь и добавляет наблюдение как другой. Предварительное знание не заявлено; отрицание наблюдения противоречит эксперименту; весь словесный инструктаж не отвергается.

hints.ru: Различите пользу метода и его обязательность.

hints.en: Observers improved while keeping their own hands still.
hints.ru: Наблюдатели улучшили результат, не двигая руками.

typicalErrors.en: Turning a useful learning route into a necessary one.
typicalErrors.ru: Превращение полезного способа обучения в обязательный.

exercises.prompt: What is the function of the hypothetical situation in the third sentence?
exercises.passage: A reviewer praises a translation for preserving every metaphor in the source text. Yet preserving an image word for word does not always preserve its effect. If a familiar expression in one language sounds baffling in another, literal retention may produce surprise where the original offered reassurance. The reviewer’s criterion therefore needs to account for readers’ likely responses as well as verbal correspondence.
options: It proves that metaphors should be removed from every translation.
It illustrates a case in which literal correspondence could conflict with preserving the original effect.
It establishes that surprise and reassurance are identical reader responses.
It supplies a documented example from the particular translation under review.
acceptedAnswers: It illustrates a case in which literal correspondence could conflict with preserving the original effect.

explanation.en: The conditional example tests the limits of literal preservation. It neither bans metaphors, documents a real instance in the reviewed book, nor equates the explicitly contrasted effects. “If” marks a hypothetical, not an observed error.
explanation.ru: Условный пример проверяет границы буквального сохранения. Он не запрещает метафоры, не документирует реальную ошибку книги и не приравнивает противопоставленные эффекты. If означает гипотезу, а не наблюдённый факт.

hints.en: Notice that the situation is introduced conditionally.
hints.ru: Обратите внимание на условную форму ситуации.

hints.en: The same words could reassure one audience but surprise another.
hints.ru: Те же слова могут успокаивать одну аудиторию и удивлять другую.

typicalErrors.en: Treating a conditional translation example as a documented error in the reviewed book.
typicalErrors.ru: Принятие условного примера перевода за подтверждённую ошибку рецензируемой книги.

options: To criticize the keeper for deliberately leaving every window unlocked.
To establish that the observatory remains fully equipped for nightly research.
To portray how a repeated routine allows a person to sustain a sense of continuity after a place’s practical function has ended.

acceptedAnswers: To portray how a repeated routine allows a person to sustain a sense of continuity after a place’s practical function has ended.

exercises.prompt: Which statement best describes the relationship between the texts?

options: Text 2 argues that the association in Text 1 cannot be investigated further.
Text 2 disproves the species counts reported in Text 1.
Text 2 proposes a way to distinguish the explanation considered in Text 1 from an alternative influence on the observed association.

explanation.en: Matching island size would help separate size from visitation, refining a deliberately tentative explanation. Text 2 does not reject counts; Text 1 says “consistent with the possibility,” not sole cause; Text 2 explicitly proposes further investigation.

hints.en: Keep Text 1’s cautious wording and Text 2’s proposed control in view.
hints.ru: Учтите осторожную формулировку первого текста и контроль второго.

hints.en: A comparison of similarly sized islands would reduce the competing influence of size.
hints.ru: Сравнение островов сходного размера уменьшает конкурирующее влияние площади.

typicalErrors.en: Mistaking a proposed control for a denial of the observed species counts.
typicalErrors.ru: Принятие предложенного контроля за отрицание наблюдённого числа видов.

exercises.prompt: The student wants to identify a limitation on using this survey to describe all town residents’ views. Which choice best uses relevant information from the notes?
exercises.passage:
Notes:
• A town surveyed 80 residents attending its weekend cycling festival.
• Sixty-two respondents supported adding bicycle parking.
• Attendance at the festival was voluntary.
• Residents who did not attend were not surveyed.
• The survey asked about bicycle parking, not car parking.
options: Because the survey included only festival attendees, its results may not represent residents who did not attend.
The weekend cycling festival attracted at least 80 residents.
Sixty-two respondents supported adding bicycle parking.
The survey proves that all residents oppose car parking.

explanation.en: The key connects the restricted sample to the population claim. The support count and minimum attendance are true but do not explain representativeness; car-parking opposition was neither asked nor established.

The school project uses an online form, whereas the farmer wrote in a diary.

exercises.prompt: The student wants to summarize the project’s sequence without adding an unsupported explanation for the delay. Which choice best uses relevant information from the notes?
exercises.passage:
Notes:
• Engineers surveyed a possible canal route in 1842.
• The council approved the route in 1845.
• Construction began in 1847.
• The first boat traveled the completed route in 1851.
• The notes do not identify why approval took three years.
options: Construction began immediately after the survey and was finished in 1845.
Because engineers refused to revise their plans, approval was delayed until 1845.
The first boat used the canal in 1842, five years before construction began.
The route was surveyed in 1842, approved in 1845, and put under construction in 1847 before opening to boats in 1851.
acceptedAnswers: The route was surveyed in 1842, approved in 1845, and put under construction in 1847 before opening to boats in 1851.

explanation.en: The key preserves all four dated stages without inventing causation. The refusal explanation is unsupported; 1842 is the survey, not the opening; construction started in 1847, not immediately after the survey, and opening was 1851.
explanation.ru: Ключ сохраняет четыре этапа без выдуманной причины. Отказ инженеров не подтверждён; 1842 — дата исследования, не открытия; строительство началось в 1847, открытие — в 1851.

hints.en: Separate the dated events from the unknown cause of the approval delay.
hints.ru: Отделите датированные события от неизвестной причины задержки.

hints.en: The order is survey, approval, construction, first boat.
hints.ru: Порядок: исследование, одобрение, строительство, первая лодка.

typicalErrors.en: Inventing a causal story to connect documented dates.
typicalErrors.ru: Выдумывание причинного объяснения между подтверждёнными датами.

exercises.prompt: The student wants to support the claim that P used less electricity while meeting the same tested cooling threshold. Which choice best uses relevant information from the notes?
exercises.passage:
Notes:
• Two coolers were tested for six hours under the same outdoor conditions.
• Cooler P used 18 watt-hours of electricity.
• Cooler Q used 30 watt-hours.
• Both kept their contents below 5°C throughout the test.
• The test did not measure purchase price or long-term durability.
options: Q used 30 watt-hours during the six-hour test.
Both coolers stayed below 5°C for six hours, but P used 18 watt-hours compared with Q’s 30.
P used less electricity because it failed to keep its contents below 5°C.
P is cheaper to buy and will last longer than Q.
acceptedAnswers: Both coolers stayed below 5°C for six hours, but P used 18 watt-hours compared with Q’s 30.

explanation.en: The key includes both equal threshold performance and lower energy use. Price and durability are unmeasured; Q alone supplies no comparison or threshold; failure contradicts the stated performance of both coolers.
explanation.ru: Ключ сочетает одинаковое соблюдение порога с меньшим расходом энергии. Цена и долговечность не измерены; данные только Q не дают сравнения и порога; провал охлаждения противоречит результатам.

hints.ru: В цели две части: расход энергии и успешное охлаждение.

hints.ru: Используйте общий температурный порог и сравнение 18 с 30.

typicalErrors.ru: Утверждение о лучшей цене или долговечности при измерении только энергии и охлаждения.

exercises.prompt: The student wants to challenge the report’s universal claim while accurately representing the findings. Which choice best uses relevant information from the notes?
exercises.passage:
Notes:
• A report claims that airtight storage always prevents salt from forming clumps.
• Researchers tested airtight and open containers under controlled conditions.
• Dry salt remained loose in airtight containers.
• Salt containing residual moisture formed clumps even in airtight containers.
• The study examined clumping, not changes in flavor.
options: Although dry salt stayed loose, salt with residual moisture clumped even in airtight containers, showing that airtight storage did not prevent clumping in every tested case.
Airtight storage never prevents salt from clumping under any conditions.
Airtight storage changed the flavor of salt that contained residual moisture.
The researchers studied both airtight and open containers.
acceptedAnswers: Although dry salt stayed loose, salt with residual moisture clumped even in airtight containers, showing that airtight storage did not prevent clumping in every tested case.

explanation.en: The moist-salt counterexample refutes “always” while retaining the dry-salt result. Replacing “always” with “never” overstates the evidence; container types alone do not challenge the claim; flavor was not tested.
explanation.ru: Контрпример влажной соли опровергает always и сохраняет результат сухой. Замена always на never чрезмерна; перечень тары сам по себе тезис не оспаривает; вкус не исследовался.

hints.en: A universal claim needs only one valid counterexample to be challenged.
hints.ru: Для оспаривания универсального тезиса достаточно одного верного контрпримера.

hints.en: Retain the distinction between dry salt and salt with residual moisture.
hints.ru: Сохраните различие между сухой солью и солью с остаточной влагой.

typicalErrors.en: Replacing an unsupported “always” claim with an equally unsupported “never” claim.
typicalErrors.ru: Замена недоказанного «всегда» столь же недоказанным «никогда».

exercises.prompt: The student wants to show why a lower average demand should not be confused with a lower peak demand. Which choice best uses relevant information from the notes?
exercises.passage:
Notes:
• A studio compared the electricity demand of two lighting systems over a rehearsal.
• System A: average demand 420 watts; highest recorded demand 700 watts.
• System B: average demand 360 watts; highest recorded demand 780 watts.
• Average demand and highest demand describe different features of use.
• The rehearsal length was the same for both tests.
options: System A used 420 watts on average during the rehearsal.
The two systems were tested for rehearsals of different lengths, making all comparisons impossible.
System B had lower average and peak demands than System A.
System B had the lower average demand, 360 rather than 420 watts, but the higher peak, 780 rather than 700 watts.
acceptedAnswers: System B had the lower average demand, 360 rather than 420 watts, but the higher peak, 780 rather than 700 watts.

explanation.en: The crossed comparison demonstrates the distinction with both metrics. A’s average alone does not do so; B’s peak is higher, not lower; equal test lengths directly contradict the last choice.
explanation.ru: Перекрёстное сравнение двух показателей демонстрирует различие. Одного среднего A недостаточно; пик B выше, не ниже; одинаковая длительность прямо опровергает последний вариант.

hints.en: Compare systems separately for average demand and highest demand.
hints.ru: Сравните системы отдельно по среднему и максимальному потреблению.

hints.en: B ranks lower on the average but higher on the peak.
hints.ru: B ниже по среднему, но выше по пику.

typicalErrors.en: Assuming that a lower average necessarily means a lower maximum.
typicalErrors.ru: Предположение, что меньшее среднее обязательно означает меньший максимум.

• The test conditions were the same for the two stone types.
• The researchers recommend considering stone type before selecting the method.
options: The researchers tested two types of stone under the same conditions.
The method reduced limestone loss from 12 to 4 milligrams and is therefore suitable for all stone.
Because the method reduced loss on limestone but increased it on sandstone, the researchers recommend considering stone type before using it.
Sandstone loss decreased by 4 milligrams, proving the method helps both materials.
acceptedAnswers: Because the method reduced loss on limestone but increased it on sandstone, the researchers recommend considering stone type before using it.

explanation.en: The key integrates the opposed outcomes and connects them to the recommendation. Limestone alone cannot justify all-stone suitability; the study description omits results; sandstone rose by 4 milligrams rather than falling.

explanation.en: The first clause has subject “team” and verb “packed”; the second has subject “second” and verb “held.” A semicolon joins these independent clauses despite commas inside the first list. exercises.passage: The turbines on the ridge automatically respond to changes in wind speed. When the wind becomes too strong, _____ blades turn to reduce the force acting on the machinery.

explanation.en: The blades belong to plural “turbines,” so the possessive determiner “their” fits. “They’re” means they are and cannot modify “blades”; “its” is singular; “it’s” means it is/has and is neither plural nor possessive.

exercises.passage: Working from a fragmentary fossil, the team not only identified several previously overlooked bones but also _____ the arrangement of the animal’s jaw. The reconstruction suggested a different feeding motion from the one proposed earlier.

explanation.en: “Not only ... but also ...” coordinates two past-tense verbs sharing “the team”: identified and reconstructed. A participle, infinitive, or noun phrase does not match that structure.
explanation.ru: Not only ... but also ... соединяет два глагола прошедшего времени с общим the team: identified и reconstructed. Причастие, инфинитив и именная группа не соответствуют структуре.

hints.en: Identify the grammatical form following “not only.”
hints.ru: Определите форму после not only.

hints.en: The second action must be parallel to “identified.”
hints.ru: Второе действие должно быть параллельно identified.

explanation.en: The three list items each contain a name and a comma-marked description. Semicolons separate these internally punctuated items consistently, as the later semicolon before “and Tessa” shows. A comma blurs item boundaries; a colon wrongly introduces the second item as an explanation; no mark leaves the items unseparated.

explanation.en: The subject is the entire singular content clause “That some diagrams appear in only one of those copies,” so “poses” agrees. The plural “diagrams” is the subject inside that clause, not the subject of the main verb. All other choices incorrectly use plural agreement for the main predicate.

hints.en: Locate the subject of the main clause, not just the nearest plural noun.

exercises.passage: The survey report includes a list of rock samples recovered from several slopes, with each entry giving a location and a brief description. The list, together with photographs showing where the samples were found, _____ researchers to revisit the exact collection sites.

explanation.en: The subject is singular “list”; “together with photographs...” adds a supplement rather than creating an “and” compound subject. “Enables” is finite and singular. “Enable” and “have enabled” are plural here; “enabling” leaves the main clause without a finite verb.
explanation.ru: Подлежащее — единственное list; together with photographs добавляет уточнение, не соединяет подлежащие союзом and. Enables — личная форма единственного числа. Enable и have enabled здесь множественные; enabling оставляет главную часть без личного сказуемого.

hints.en: Remove the comma-enclosed “together with” phrase.
hints.ru: Уберите заключённую в запятые часть together with.

hints.en: The core is “The list enables researchers...”.
hints.ru: Основа: The list enables researchers... .

typicalErrors.en: Treating “together with” as though it formed a plural compound subject with “and.”

exercises.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to Standard English conventions?
exercises.passage: Several technicians offered suggestions while the machine was being assembled, but one resolved the persistent alignment problem. The engineer to _____ the team later sent its thanks had proposed a small change to the supporting frame.

explanation.en: The pronoun is the object of the preposition “to” placed before the relative clause, requiring formal object form “whom.” “Who” is a subject form; “whose” expresses possession but has no following possessed noun; “who’s” expands to who is/has and breaks the clause.
explanation.ru: Местоимение — дополнение предлога to перед относительной частью: нужна объектная форма whom. Who — субъектная; whose выражает принадлежность без нужного существительного; who’s = who is/has и нарушает предложение.

hints.en: Identify the pronoun’s role after the fronted preposition.
hints.ru: Определите роль местоимения после вынесенного предлога.

hints.en: The team sent thanks to that engineer, making the pronoun an object.
hints.ru: Команда отправила благодарность тому инженеру: местоимение — дополнение.

typicalErrors.ru: Использование субъектной формы относительного местоимения после вынесенного предлога to.

exercises.passage: The laboratory compared the spectral readings produced by a new sensor with readings from a calibrated reference sensor. After adjustment, the new sensor’s readings were nearly identical to _____ across the range of wavelengths tested.

explanation.en: The comparison is plural readings with plural readings, expressed by “those of.” Comparing readings to the physical sensor mixes categories; “that” is singular and cannot replace plural “readings”; “sensor’s being” supplies neither a grammatical nor meaningful comparison.
explanation.ru: Сравниваются множественные показания с показаниями: those of. Сравнение показаний с физическим датчиком смешивает категории; that — единственное число вместо readings; sensor’s being не даёт осмысленного грамматического сравнения.

exercises.passage: The maritime archive recently moved to a building twice the size of its former home. Although _____ now able to display more objects, the archive continues to devote most of its space to preserving records that visitors rarely see.

explanation.en: The subordinate clause needs “it is,” contracted to “it’s,” before “now able.” “Its” is a possessive determiner, “its’” is nonstandard, and “it” alone leaves the clause without a finite verb. The nearby phrase “its former home” does not determine the blank’s grammatical role.
explanation.ru: Придаточной части нужно it is, сокращённо it’s, перед now able. Its выражает принадлежность, its’ ненормативно, а it без is оставляет часть без сказуемого. Соседнее its former home не определяет роль пропуска.

hints.en: Expand any proposed contraction and read the whole subordinate clause.
hints.ru: Раскройте возможное сокращение и прочтите придаточную часть целиком.

hints.en: The meaning is “Although it is now able...”.
hints.ru: Смысл: Although it is now able... .

typicalErrors.ru: Перенос соседней притяжательной формы в часть, где нужно сокращение it is.

exercises.passage: The excavation revealed a stone walkway beneath several later building foundations. By the time the last of those buildings was constructed, two _____ had passed since the walkway was first laid across the site.

explanation.en: “Two centuries” is the plural subject of “had passed” and expresses no possession, so it takes no apostrophe. “Century’s” is singular possessive; “centuries’” is plural possessive without anything possessed here; “centuries’s” is nonstandard.
explanation.ru: Two centuries — множественное подлежащее при had passed, не принадлежность, поэтому без апострофа. Century’s — единственная притяжательная форма; centuries’ выражает ненужную здесь принадлежность; centuries’s ненормативно.

hints.en: Determine whether the time expression owns something or acts as the subject.
hints.ru: Определите, выражает ли время принадлежность или служит подлежащим.

hints.en: The centuries themselves “had passed.”
hints.ru: Именно века had passed.

typicalErrors.ru: Добавление апострофа к обычному множественному существительному в роли подлежащего.

exercises.passage: In the shallow tank, a small octopus repeatedly opened a jar to reach food placed inside it. The octopus, which gripped the jar with several _____ its remaining arms to turn the lid until it loosened.

explanation.en: The nonrestrictive relative clause beginning “which” must close with a comma after “arms.” The main predicate is “used its remaining arms.” No closing comma misjoins the clauses; semicolon and colon incorrectly split the main subject from its predicate.
explanation.ru: Неограничительное относительное придаточное с which закрывается запятой после arms. Главное сказуемое — used its remaining arms. Без запятой части неверно сливаются; точка с запятой и двоеточие отделяют главное подлежащее от сказуемого.

hints.ru: Различите глагол относительного придаточного и главный глагол.

hints.en: Remove “which gripped the jar with several arms” to expose the main clause.
hints.ru: Уберите which gripped the jar with several arms, чтобы увидеть главную часть.

typicalErrors.ru: Незакрытое неограничительное придаточное с which перед главным сказуемым.

exercises.passage: The inscriptions on the two stones were worn, and several symbols were difficult to distinguish in ordinary photographs. After comparing paper rubbings made under the same conditions, _____
options: there was a small difference between the final symbols, the researchers found.
a small difference between the final symbols became apparent to the researchers.
the researchers identified a small difference between the final symbols.
the final symbols revealed a small difference to the researchers.
acceptedAnswers: the researchers identified a small difference between the final symbols.

explanation.en: The introductory action “comparing” must attach to the people who performed it: “the researchers.” In the distractors, a difference, symbols, or dummy “there” occupies the subject position and cannot logically perform that comparison. Mentioning researchers later does not repair the attachment.
explanation.ru: Начальное comparing должно относиться к сравнивавшим людям: the researchers. В дистракторах место подлежащего занимают различие, символы или формальное there, неспособные сравнивать. Позднее упоминание исследователей связь не исправляет.

hints.en: Identify the agent performing the comparison, regardless of where that agent is mentioned.
hints.ru: Определите исполнителя сравнения независимо от места его упоминания.

hints.en: The people who compare must immediately follow the introductory modifier as the subject.
hints.ru: Сравнивающие люди должны стать подлежащим сразу после начального оборота.

typicalErrors.en: Assuming that naming the researchers later repairs a dangling introductory modifier.
typicalErrors.ru: Предположение, что позднее упоминание исследователей исправляет неверно присоединённый начальный оборот.

exercises.passage: During the trial, the scheduling software grouped deliveries to nearby addresses before assigning them to drivers, thereby _____ the number of times a vehicle had to cross the city. The company measured the change over a full working week.

explanation.en: “Thereby” introduces a participial phrase showing the result of the preceding action: “thereby reducing.” The finite forms “reduced,” “reduces,” and “has reduced” lack a subject and valid independent-clause connection in this position.
explanation.ru: Thereby вводит причастный оборот результата: thereby reducing. Личные формы reduced, reduces и has reduced в этой позиции не имеют подлежащего и корректной связи самостоятельной части.

hints.en: Determine whether the final phrase is a new main clause or a result modifier.
hints.ru: Определите, является ли финал новой главной частью или оборотом результата.

hints.en: After “thereby,” use the -ing form to describe the effect of grouping deliveries.
hints.ru: После thereby используйте форму -ing для результата группировки доставок.

A. In the fictional town of Lanton, a college began a roof-garden trial in 2022. Three low buildings received planted roof trays, while three similar buildings kept their existing roofs. Each building carried a temperature sensor beneath the roof surface. Staff recorded readings at noon for eight summer weeks.

B. On clear days, the planted roofs were cooler beneath the surface than the comparison roofs. On cloudy days, the difference was smaller. The team did not measure indoor electricity use, so the readings alone cannot establish how much energy the gardens saved. Nor did the trial compare different plant species.

C. Maintaining the trays required more time than the college expected. Volunteers initially watered them by hand, but the college later installed a drip system. The team plans to repeat the measurements in winter before recommending the same design for every college building.
exercises.evidence: Three low buildings received planted roof trays, while three similar buildings kept their existing roofs.

explanation.en: Paragraph C connects extra maintenance effort, a watering change and planned winter testing.
explanation.ru: Абзац C объединяет дополнительные работы, смену полива и план зимней проверки.

A. The fictional Reedbank seed library opened inside a public library in 2021. Gardeners may borrow packets of seeds without a fee. They are encouraged, but not required, to return seeds collected from their harvest. Each returned packet must identify the plant and the year of collection.

B. At first, volunteers arranged packets alphabetically. Visitors unfamiliar with plant names found this difficult, so the library replaced that arrangement with groups based on planting season. The change did not increase the number of packets the shelves could hold, but it helped visitors locate suitable seeds.

C. A university team is studying the scheme. Its first interviews involved people who had borrowed seeds; people who had never used the library were not interviewed. Most interviewees valued the opportunity to try unfamiliar vegetables. The researchers caution that these interviews cannot show whether the scheme changes gardening habits across the whole town. They plan a wider household survey next year.

exercises.passage:
A. The fictional Fenmere museum owns a tower clock removed from a demolished station. For many years, visitors saw only its decorated face. During a recent conservation project, staff placed the mechanism behind a transparent panel so visitors could see how the gears interact. The clock now runs for ten minutes each hour to limit wear.

B. Conservators found two replacement gears whose metal differed from that of the original mechanism. A maintenance notebook confirmed that repairs had been made in 1911, but it did not identify which components were replaced. The team therefore describes the gears as later additions without assigning them a precise date.

C. Rather than polish every surface, conservators retained marks left by earlier workers. These traces can provide evidence about past maintenance. Staff also produced a digital model, allowing visitors to rotate the mechanism on a screen. The model improves access to hidden parts, but it cannot reproduce the sound of the running clock. A separate recording supplies that experience.
exercises.evidence: The fictional Fenmere museum owns a tower clock removed from a demolished station.

explanation.en: The material difference concerns the metal, not an exact repair date.
